text.title: Growth Loops Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when applying Growth Loops. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Detector clauses make them mechanically catchable.

antipattern.symptom: The diagram has an arrow from "retained user" back to "acquisition" but no event exists where a retained user produces a new user; the projection compounds anyway.

root-cause.source: Brian Balfour, Reforge, 'Growth Loops are the New Funnels' (2018)

antipattern.root-cause: The fuel-back stage was drawn, not instrumented; the spec never named the reinvestment event.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-loop-closes-output-into-input`: require the tracked fuel-back event and the same unit at both ends; otherwise label the design a funnel and stop the projection.

antipattern.symptom: Month one shows 300 loop-sourced sign-ups; the projection multiplies by twelve, or compounds the first cycle's k forever; month four comes in at a third of plan.

root-cause.source: Andrew Chen, The Cold Start Problem (2021)

antipattern.root-cause: No decay term and no saturation ceiling; the projection window was shorter than three cycles.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-steady-state-projection-90-days`: cohort-by-cohort model over at least 90 days and three cycles with explicit decay for the loop type.

antipattern.symptom: The metrics table shows a 25 percent share rate with no date and no sample; the real event, once instrumented, reads 3 percent; every projection was off by an order of magnitude.

root-cause.source: Widely established practice in growth analytics

antipattern.root-cause: Stage rates were filled from benchmarks or intuition and never flagged as assumptions.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-stage-conversion-measured-not-estimated`: each stage carries an event, a date and a sample size, or is flagged `assumption` with the flag surfaced in the projection headline.

antipattern.symptom: The spec reports k of 0.6 and describes the loop as self-sustaining; the paid budget is cut on the strength of it; growth stops with the spend.
antipattern.root-cause: The amplifier reading of k below 1 (multiplier 1 / (1 - k)) was not distinguished from viral growth.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-loop-efficiency-and-cycle-time`: below 1, present the loop as a multiplier on external inputs; above 1, bound the growth rate by cycle time.

antipattern.symptom: Three experiments in a row target the invite email at 45 percent open rate while the invitee landing page converts at 6 percent and is untouched.
antipattern.root-cause: The friction map did not name a bottleneck, so teams optimised the stage they controlled.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-friction-map-names-the-bottleneck`: name the lowest-conversion stage, quantify the doubling effect, and rank the experiment backlog on it.

antipattern.symptom: Invitations per user triple; loop-sourced users activate at half the baseline rate; the sending domain lands on a blocklist, or the programmatic pages stop being indexed.

root-cause.source: Andrew Chen, The Cold Start Problem (2021); Google Search Central, 'Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content'

antipattern.root-cause: k was the only metric; no quality guardrail existed on the loop's output.
antipattern.fix: Enforce rule `r-loop-quality-guardrail`: numeric activation and retention (or index and traffic) threshold on loop output; revert any optimisation that breaches it.

section.title: Human checkpoint
section.p: Before any binding action driven by a Growth Loops output (reallocating paid budget, launching loop experiments, changing incentive mechanics), a named human reviewer must sign off. The agent surfaces a `ready_for_review=true` flag and does NOT auto-commit decisions, copy, configs, or rollouts.
